children: Asian currencies consolidate against dollar, but still face pressure from expectations of Fed rate hikes, which tend to enhance the appeal of U.S. fixed-income assets and buoy demand for the greenback. FOMC minutes indicated that nearly all members agreed in October that they would have to raise rates in the months ahead, CBA's Joseph Capurso says in a report. The minutes also showed that two members said an increase of more than 25 bps could be warranted in December, Capurso adds. The U.S. dollar is little changed at 159.40 yen and steady at 1,332.54 won, while the Australian dollar is flat at US$0.6715, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
